For a matrix $$[M]=\begin{bmatrix} \frac{3}{5} & \frac{4}{5}\\ x & \frac{3}{5} \end{bmatrix}$$
  the transpose of the matrix is equal to the inverse of the matrix $[M]^{T}= [M]^{-1}$. The value of x is given by

detailed_solution.markdown:
$\text{If }\quad A^{T}=A^{-1}$

then A is orthogonal matrix.

Therefore $A . A^{-1}=A^{-1} A=I$

$\text{and }A^{T} A=A A^{T}=I$

since $\mathrm{M}$ is orthogonal matrix

$M^{T} M=I$

$$=\left[\begin{array}{cc}\frac{3}{5} & x \\ \frac{4}{5} & \frac{3}{5}\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{cc}\frac{3}{5} & \frac{4}{5} \\ x & \frac{3}{5}\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{cc}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{array}\right]$$

$$\left[\begin{aligned} \left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^{2}+x^{2} \quad\left(\frac{3}{5} \cdot \frac{4}{5}\right)+\frac{3}{5} x \\ \left(\frac{4}{5} \cdot \frac{3}{5}\right)+\frac{3}{5} \cdot x\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^{2}+\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^{2} \end{aligned} \right]$$

$$=\left[\begin{array}{cc}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{array}\right] \Rightarrow \text{Compare both sides} a_{12}$$

$a_{12}=\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)+\left(\frac{3}{5}\right) x=0$

$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{3}{5} x=-\frac{3}{5} \cdot \frac{4}{5}$

The divergence of the vector field $3xz\hat{i}+2xy\hat{j}-yz^{2}\hat{k}$
 at a point (1,1,1 ) is equal to

detailed_solution.markdown:

$\vec{f}=3 x z \hat{i}+2 x y \hat{j}-y z^{2} \hat{k}$

$\vec{f}=\left[f_{1} \hat{i}+f_{2} \hat{j}+f_{3} \hat{k}\right]$

$$\begin{aligned}&\text{Divergence of vector field} \vec{f}=\nabla \cdot \vec{f} \\ &\text{Div}(f)=\left(i \frac{\partial}{\partial x}+\hat{j} \frac{\partial}{\partial y}+\hat{k} \frac{\partial}{\partial z}\right) \cdot\left(t_{1} \hat{i}+f_{2} \hat{j}+f_{3} \hat{k}\right) \\ &\text{Div}(f)=\frac{\partial f_{1}}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial f_{2}}{\partial y}+\frac{\partial f_{3}}{\partial z} \\ &\text{Div}(f)=\frac{\partial}{\partial x}[3 x z]+\frac{\partial}{\partial y}[2 x y]+\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left[-2 y z^{2}\right] \\ &\text{Div}(f)=3 z+2 x-2 z y \\ &\text{Div}(f)|_{(1,1,1)}=3(1)+2(1)-2(1)(1)=3 \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2009:q4.title: GATE ME 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 4
pp:me:2009:q4.question: If three coins are tossed simultaneously, the probability of getting at least one head

detailed_solution.markdown:
Three coins are tossed simultaneously, the total

number of ways $=2^{3}=8$

Number of ways to get all tails = 1

$Probability to get all tails$

$=\frac{\text { Number of ways for tails }}{\text { Total number of ways }}=\frac{1}{8}$

Therefore probability to get at least one head is

$=1-\frac{1}{8}=\frac{7}{8}$

or, Total number of ways with at least one head is

$$\left.\begin{matrix} & &\left.\begin{array}{lll} H & T & T \\ T & H & T \\ T & T & H \end{array} \right] \\ &&\left.\begin{array}{lll} H & T & T \\ T & H & T \\ T & T & H \end{array} \right] \\ &&\left.\begin{array}{lll} H & H & H \end{array} \right] \end{matrix}\right\}$$

Therefore probability to get at least one head $=\frac{7}{8}$

A coolant fluid at 30$^{\circ}$C flows over a heated flat plate maintained at a constant temperature of 100$^{\circ}$C. The boundary layer temperature distribution at a given location on the plate may be approximated as  $T=30+70 exp(-y)$
 where y (in m) is the distance normal to the plate and T is in $^{\circ}$C. If thermal conductivity of the fluid is 1.0W/mK, the local convective heat transfer coefficient (in $W/m^{2}K$) at that location will be

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{array}{l} T_{s}=100^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \text{At}\; \mathrm{y}=0 ; q_{\mathrm{cond}}=q_{\mathrm{conv}} \\ -\left.k_{f} \frac{\partial T}{\partial y}\right|_{y=0}=h \Delta T=h\left(T_{s}-T_{\infty}\right) \\ -\left.(1) \frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left[30+70 e^{-y}\right]\right|_{y=0}=h(100-30) \\ -\left.\left[0+70(-1) e^{-y}\right]\right|_{y=0}=h(70) \\ 70 e^{-0}=h(70) \\ ^{0} \mathrm{h}=1 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \mathrm{K} \end{array}$$ Alternatively Given data: $$\begin{aligned} T_{\infty}&=30^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ T_{s}&=100^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ k_{f}&=1 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{mK} \\ T&=30+70 \exp (-y) \end{aligned}$$ Differentiating w.r.t y, we get $$\begin{aligned} \text{At }\quad y &=0\\ \frac{d T}{d y}&=-70 e^{-y}\\ \left(\frac{d T}{d y}\right)^{y=0}&=-70 \end{aligned}$$ We know that local convective heat transfer coefficient: $h_{x}=\frac{-k_{1}\left(\frac{d T}{d y}\right)_{y=0}}{T_{s}-T_{\infty}}=\frac{-1 \times(-70)}{100-30}=1 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \mathrm{K}$

primary.subtopicLabel: First Law, Heat, Work and Energy

detailed_solution.concept: Refrigeration and Air-conditioning - Vapor and Gas Refrigeration
detailed_solution.markdown: Given data: $$\begin{aligned} h_{2} &=283 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ h_{3} &=116 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ &=h_{4} \\ h_{1} &=232 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}$$ Coefficient of performance, $$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{COP} &=\frac{\text { Refrigerating effect: Re }}{\text { Work input: } w} \\ \text { where } \mathrm{Re} &=h_{1}-h_{4}=232-116 \\ &=116 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg}\\ \text { and } \quad w &=h_{2}-h_{1}=283-232 \\ &=51 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ \therefore \quad \mathrm{COP} &=\frac{116}{51}=2.27 \end{aligned}$$

detailed_solution.markdown: Cold Shut: Two stream of liquid metal which are not hot enough to fuse properly result into a casting defect known as cold shut OR For a casting with gates at its two sides, the misrun may show up at the centre of the casting. When this happens, the defect is called a cold shut. Swell: This defect is found on the vertical surface of a casting if the moulding sand is deformed by the hydrostatic pressure caused by the high moisture content in the sand. Wash: A low projection on the drag surface of a casting commencing near the gate is called a wash. This is caused by erosion of sand due to the high velocity jet of liquid metal in bottom gating. pp:me:2009:q20.title: GATE ME 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 20
pp:me:2009:q20.question: Which of the following forecasting methods takes a fraction of forecast error into account for the next period forecast?

detailed_solution.concept: Industrial Engineering - Production Planning and Control
detailed_solution.markdown:
Exponential smoothing methods of forecasting takes a fraction of forecast error into account for next period forecast

$$\begin{aligned} F_{t}&=F_{t-1}+\alpha\left(D_{t-1}-F_{t-1}\right) \\ F_{t}&=F_{t-1}+\alpha e_{t} \end{aligned}$$

where, $F_{t}$ is the forecast at time t

$D_{t}$ is the actual demand at time t

$F_{t-1}$ is the forecast at time t-1

$\alpha$ is the smoothing coefficient

$e_{t}=D_{t-1}-F_{t-1}$ is forecast error

The value of $\alpha$ varies between 0 and 1, with commonly used value of 0.01 to 0.30 .

New estimate = Old estimate of latest actual demand $+\alpha$ [latest actual demand - old estimate of latest actual demand]

Exponential smoothing provides a convenient, systematic and recursive method of revisiting the forecast for the next period whenever discrepancy exists between the previously forecast demand for current period and the actual demand for current period.

pp:me:2009:q22.question:
The solution of $x\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+y=x^{4}$
  with the condition $y(1)=\frac{6}{5}$

detailed_solution.markdown:
Given differential equation is

Standard form

$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}+P y=Q$

where P and Q function of x only and solution is given by

$y(\text { I.F. })=\int Q \cdot(I F .) d x+C$

where, integrating factor (I.F.)$=e^{\int P d x}$

$\text{Here} \quad P =\frac{1}{x} \text { and } Q=x^{3}$

given condition

$y(1)=\frac{6}{5}$

means at $x=1 ; y=\frac{6}{5}$

$\Rightarrow \quad y=\frac{x^{4}}{5}+\frac{1}{x}$

Incompressible flow satisfy continuity equation

$\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial v}{\partial y}=0$

$P. u=2 y, v=-3 x$

Incompressible flow $\Rightarrow \quad 0+0=0$

$Q. u=3 x y, v=0$

$\frac{\partial(3 x y)}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial(0)}{\partial y}$

Compressible flow $\Rightarrow 3 y+0 \neq 0$

$R. u=-2 x, v=2 y$

$\frac{\partial(-2 x)}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial(2 y)}{\partial y}$

Incompressible flow

$-2+2=0$

For irrotational flow condition is

$$\begin{aligned} \omega_{2} &=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial u}{\partial y}\right)=0 \\ \text { For P:} \quad & u=2 y, v=-3 x \\ & \omega_{2}=\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{\partial(-3 x)}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial(2 y)}{\partial y}\right] \\ &=\frac{1}{2}[-3-2] \neq 0 \;\;\;\text{   (Rotational flow)}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} \text{For Q: }\quad u &=3 x y, v=0 \\ \omega_{2} &=\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{\partial(0)}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial(3 x y)}{\partial y}\right] \\ &=\frac{1}{2}[0-3 x] \neq 0 \;\;\;\text{   (Rotational flow)} \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} \text{For R: }\quad u &=-2 x, v=2 y \\ \omega_{2} &=\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{\partial(2 y)}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial(-2 x)}{\partial y}\right] \\ &=\frac{1}{2}[0-0]=0 \; \; \; \text{  (Irrotational flow)}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} \text { Diameter: } d&=30 \mathrm{mm} \\ F_{\max }&=+160 \mathrm{kN} \text { (Tension) } \\ F_{\min }&=-40 \mathrm{kN} \text { (Compression) } \\ \text { Tensile strength: } S_{u}&=600 \mathrm{MPa} \\ \text { Yield strength: } S_{y}&=430 \mathrm{MPa}\\ \text{Corrected endurance,}\\ S_{e}&=240 \mathrm{MPa} \end{aligned}$$

Stress amplitude,

detailed_solution.concept: Strength of Materials - Bending of Beams
detailed_solution.markdown: For arm AB: At ant section X-X, at a distance x frome A $$\begin{aligned} M_{x} &=-P x \\ U_{A B} &=\int \frac{M_{x}^{2} d x}{2 E I}=\int_{0}^{L} \frac{(-P x)^{2}}{2 E I} d x \\ U_{A B} &=\frac{P^{2}}{2 E I}\left(\frac{x^{3}}{3}\right)_{0}^{L}=\frac{P^{2} L^{3}}{6 E I} \end{aligned}$$ For arm BC: $$\begin{aligned} R_{B}+R_{C} &=0 \\ M_{C} &=0 \\ R_{B} L-P L &=0 \\ R_{B} &=P \\ R_{C} &=-P \\ M_{x} &=R_{C} x=P_{x} \\ U_{B C} &=\int_{0}^{L} \frac{M_{x}^{2} d x}{2 E I}=\int_{0}^{L} \frac{P^{2} x^{2} d x}{2 E I} \\ &=\frac{P^{2} L^{3}}{6 E I} \end{aligned}$$ Total strain energy sotred in the frame of two arm $$\begin{array}{l} U=U_{A B}+U_{B C} \\ U=\frac{P^{2} L^{3}}{6 E I}+\frac{P^{2} L^{3}}{6 E I}=\frac{P^{2} L^{3}}{3 E I} \end{array}$$ Therefore, vertical deflection of A is $\delta_{A}=\frac{\partial U}{\partial P}=\frac{\partial}{\partial P}\left[\frac{P^{2} L^{3}}{3 E I}\right]=\frac{2 P L^{3}}{3 E I}$

pp:me:2009:q46.title: GATE ME 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 46
pp:me:2009:q46.question: Minimum shear strain in orthogonal turning with a cutting tool of zero rake angle is

detailed_solution.concept: Manufacturing Engineering - Machining and Machine Tool Operation
detailed_solution.markdown:
During orthogonal machining.

Shear strain: $\gamma=\cot \phi+\tan (\phi-\alpha)$

Cutting tool having rake angle: $\alpha=0^{\circ}$

then $\quad \gamma=\cot \phi+\tan \phi$

For minimum value of shea

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{d \gamma}{d \phi} &=\frac{d}{d \phi}(\cot \phi+\tan \phi)=0 \\ \frac{d \gamma}{d \phi} &=-\operatorname{cosec}^{2} \phi+\sec ^{2} \phi=0\\ -\frac{1}{\sin ^{2} \phi}+\frac{1}{\cos ^{2} \phi} &=0 \\ \Rightarrow \frac{\cos ^{2} \phi-\sin ^{2} \phi}{\cos ^{2} \phi \sin ^{2} \phi}&=0 \\ \Rightarrow \cos 2 \phi=0=\cos \frac{\pi}{2}&=\cos \frac{3 \pi}{2} \\ \Rightarrow \phi &= \frac{\pi}{4}\\ \frac{d^{2} \gamma}{d \phi^{2}}&=-2 \text{cosec} \phi \cdot(-\operatorname{cosec} \phi \cot \phi) \\ &+2\sec\phi.(\sec\phi\tan\phi)\\ \frac{d^{2} \gamma}{d \phi^{2}}&=2 \text{cosec}^{2} \phi \cot \phi+2 \sec ^{2} \phi\\ \left.\frac{d^{2} \gamma}{d \phi^{2}}\right|_{a+\phi=\frac{\pi}{4}}& \gt 0 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore $\gamma$ is minimum at $\phi=\frac{\pi}{4}$

Therefore minimum shear strain $\gamma$ is given by

$$\begin{aligned} \gamma &=\cot \frac{\pi}{4}+\tan \frac{\pi}{4} \\ &=2^{\circ} \end{aligned}$$
